subject: Maths
title: Surface area of prisms
subtitle: Volume and Surface Area · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the surface area of prisms by finding the area of each face.

key_vocab.definition: A prism is a 3D shape with a uniform cross-section. Its surface area is the sum of the areas of all its faces: two identical end faces plus the rectangular side faces.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the surface area of prisms by finding the area of each face.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: prism -- A prism is a 3D shape with a uniform cross-section. Its surface area is the sum of the areas of all its faces: two identical end faces plus the rectangular side faces.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Surface area of a prism = 2 times the end face area plus the lateral (side) area. The lateral area equals perimeter of cross-section times length.
SA = 2A + P × l
A = area of end face, P = perimeter of end, l = length of prism

Key examples:
  ✓ Cuboid: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh)  (three pairs of rectangular faces)
  ✓ Triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles  (count all faces)
  ✓ SA = 2A + Ph (A = end area, P = perimeter, h = length)  (general prism formula)
  ✗ SA = area of cross-section × length  (that gives volume, not surface area)
  ✗ A triangular prism has 4 faces  (it has 5 faces: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – cuboid
  Find the surface area of a cuboid 6 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
  Three pairs of faces: 6×4 = 24, 6×3 = 18, 4×3 = 12
  Double each: 48 + 36 + 24
  SA = 108 cm²
  108 cm²
  (A cuboid has three different pairs of rectangular faces.)

Example 2 – triangular prism
  A triangular prism has a right-angled triangle cross-section (base 6, height 8, hypotenuse 10 cm) and length 12 cm. Find the SA.
  Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48 cm²
  Three rectangles: 6×12 + 8×12 + 10×12 = 72 + 96 + 120 = 288 cm²
  SA = 48 + 288 = 336 cm²
  336 cm²
  (Find all five faces: two triangles and three rectangles.)

sections.title: Cuboids
sections.content:
Find the surface area of each cuboid.

(a) 5 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm
(b) 8 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm
(c) 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm
(d) 7 cm × 7 cm × 7 cm

sections.title: Triangular prisms
sections.content:
Find the surface area of each triangular prism.

(a) Triangle: base 6, height 4, hyp 5 cm. Length 10 cm.
(b) Triangle: base 8, height 3, hyp 5 cm. Length 12 cm.
(c) Triangle: base 5, height 12, hyp 13 cm. Length 8 cm.
(d) Equilateral triangle side 6 cm. Length 10 cm.

sections.title: Using SA = 2A + Pl
sections.content:
Given the cross-section area A, perimeter P, and length l, find the SA.

(a) A = 15 cm², P = 20 cm, l = 8 cm
(b) A = 24 cm², P = 22 cm, l = 10 cm
(c) A = 30 cm², P = 28 cm, l = 6 cm
(d) A = 18 cm², P = 18 cm, l = 12 cm

sections.title: Trapezoidal prisms
sections.content:
Find the surface area of each trapezoidal prism.

(a) Parallel sides 4, 8 cm; height 3 cm; slant sides 5 cm each; length 10 cm
(b) Parallel sides 6, 10 cm; height 4 cm; slant sides 5 cm each; length 12 cm
(c) Parallel sides 3, 7 cm; height 3 cm; slant sides 4 cm each; length 9 cm
(d) Parallel sides 5, 11 cm; height 4 cm; slant sides 5 cm each; length 14 cm

sections.title: Mixed prism problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Cube with side 5 cm. SA?
(b) Triangular prism: isosceles triangle base 10, equal sides 13, height 12 cm. Length 20 cm.
(c) Cuboid SA = 340 cm². If l = 10, w = 5, find h.
(d) A pentagonal prism: end area 45 cm², perimeter 30 cm, length 8 cm.
(e) Hexagonal prism: end area 54 cm², perimeter 36 cm, length 10 cm.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ SA of a prism = 2 × end area + perimeter × length
✗ SA of a prism = cross-section area × length
✓ A triangular prism has 5 faces
✗ All faces of a prism are rectangles
✓ To find SA you must add the area of every single face
